translation_notes: prefixes: DCTERMS->dcterms, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, OA->oa, SCHEMA->schema, SV->sv

Runs against the REAL installed apysource 0.10.0 (load_yaml, namespaces) on both sides; no logic is re-implemented. Only `_write_yaml`, a module-level test helper the region calls, is transcribed verbatim into original.py/translated.ldpy.

`from apysource.namespaces import oa:, schema:, sv:` fails against the real module (ImportError: cannot import name '__namespaces__'): the package defines SV/OA/SCHEMA as rdflib Namespaces but no `__namespaces__` registry, which a prefix import reads at run time. Finding: `from m import p:` works only on modules written for it (ldpy modules, or ones with a registry); on an ordinary project namespaces module a two-line shim is needed. apysource_ns_shim.py re-exports the package's own objects and adds the registry; classification minor-restructuring for that reason.
`from rdflib.namespace import DCTERMS, RDF, RDFS` cannot take `from … import p:` (ldpy/012 point 21); only RDF is dereferenced, so `@prefix rdf:` covers it.
`g.subjects(RDF.type, SV.Source)` -> `m{ ?s rdf:type sv:Source }(g)` (one pattern, one projected variable, bare terms; sorted() makes the order irrelevant).

Proof: the region only asserts and returns None, so driver.py gives it a tmp_path whose write_text stores chosen content: (1) same YAML twice -> passes; (2) YAML differing only in a fragment label -> passes (a pattern widened to any typed subject then raises); (3) a second source -> AssertionError (a pattern narrowed to another class then passes). Checked by breaking the translation: widened `?s rdf:type ?t` -> FAIL (call[1] None vs AssertionError); narrowed `sv:Fragment` -> FAIL (call[1] and call[2] outcomes swap); restored -> OK.
